body:
Chief: F1 IS A REAL CONFLICT AND IT IS WITH MY OWN REASONING. RULING: OPTION (b), AND I HAVE TO CORRECT SOMETHING I SAID TWO HOURS AGO.

THE CONFLICT, restated because the example settles it: source "Alpha beta.", token [0,5), sentence [0,11). At ReaderAt(5) the token is fully read and the sentence is not. Under the full-span rule Tokens emits the token, Sentences emits nothing, and clipping into a prefix unit is correctly forbidden. So the token is OnMark with no ancestor at the coarser surface level. AND THIS IS NOT AN EDGE CASE - every multi-token sentence has such horizons, which is to say every ordinary reading position.

WHERE THE CONFLICT CAME FROM: ME. When I ruled cumulative Tokens I wrote that it was "FORCED, not preferred - V-L1 requires every child to have a visible ancestor at a coarser level." V-L1 WAS WRITTEN FOR THE NARRATIVE LEVEL HIERARCHY - Story, Episode, Scene, Event. I extended it to the surface axis in a single sentence, without checking whether it survives a reading horizon. It does not, and collab found that by construction rather than by fixture.

RULING - OPTION (b), WITH THE SCOPE STATED PRECISELY. V-L1 IS A PROPERTY OF THE LEVEL HIERARCHY AT A GIVEN HORIZON, OVER THE UNITS THAT HORIZON ADMITS. IT DOES NOT REQUIRE THE HORIZON TO ADMIT ANCESTORS. A token whose sentence is not yet complete is OffProjection at Sentences - and that is not a violation, IT IS V-L2 WORKING. OffProjection is already a legal, typed outcome precisely so that "this address is not represented here" can be said honestly rather than faked with a clipped prefix.

WHY NOT (a), which collab recommended and which I take seriously because it is the conservative choice: hierarchical closure would HIDE THE TOKEN THE READER HAS ACTUALLY READ in order to preserve an ancestor that they have not. That inverts the horizon's meaning. The horizon exists to show the reader what they have seen and no more; suppressing something they HAVE seen because its container is incomplete withholds their own evidence from them. Under (a), token detail appears only after the containing sentence completes - which for the "fly the story" requirement means the finest grain is unavailable exactly while you are reading.

WHY NOT (c): weakening the full-span rule means clipping a unit into a prefix, and a half-token with a stable id is a lie about the SurfaceAtlas.

WHAT I OWE, since the reasoning I gave for cumulative Tokens is now gone: CUMULATIVE TOKENS STILL STANDS, ON DIFFERENT AND SMALLER GROUNDS. At a fixed horizon, Tokens including Sentences is a ZOOM-LEVEL property - finer detail shows the coarser grain too, so the reader sees structure at both. That is a design choice with a good reason, not a law forcing it. I over-claimed and I am withdrawing the force while keeping the decision.

REQUIRED IN THE CANDIDATE, and collab is right that it is needed whichever ruling won: A MID-SENTENCE CAPACITY LAW. At a horizon strictly inside a sentence, assert that Tokens emits the completed tokens, Sentences emits no partial sentence, and the address resolves OffProjection at Sentences rather than OnMark or ViaAncestor. Then mutate: a clipped prefix sentence must fail, and hierarchical closure must fail. Both directions, because the law now has two ways to be wrong.

ENGINEER: this changes what you build. F2 - the SurfaceAtlas parent law being weaker than the design assumes - I am reading now and will rule separately; do not start on the parent chain until I do.

collab: read-only, no claim, found a normative conflict by construction rather than by luck, and offered three dispositions with a recommendation and its cost. That is the most useful shape a review can take.
